title: Randomized trials of invasive cardiovascular interventions that include a placebo control: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review; 30 trials, 4102 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Heterogeneous interventions and outcomes; mixed risk of bias.
appraisal.one_line: Systematic review of placebo-controlled randomised trials of invasive cardiovascular interventions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Ten trials (33%) demonstrated statistically significant superiority of invasive interventions over placebo controls for the respective predefined primary outcomes.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the interpretation of unblinded trials of invasive procedures.

title: Pooled Analysis of PFO Occluder Device Trials in Patients With PFO and Migraine.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: IPD pooled analysis of 2 randomised trials (PRIMA, PREMIUM); 337 subjects (176 closure, 161 medical).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small trials with unblinded or inconsistently blinded designs; migraine endpoints are patient-reported.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled individual-participant analysis of two Amplatzer trials: PFO closure reduced migraine days and attacks versus medical therapy.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Met 3 of 4 efficacy endpoints: mean reduction of monthly migraine days (-3.1 days vs. -1.9 days; p = 0.02), monthly attacks (-2.0 vs. -1.4; p = 0.01) and complete cessation (14 [9%] vs. 1 [0.7%]; p < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adjacent PFO closure indication in migraine.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion during Cardiac Surgery to Prevent Stroke.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised trial; 2379 occlusion and 2391 no-occlusion participants; NCT01561651.
appraisal.main_limitation: Surgical rather than percutaneous occlusion, and 76.8% continued oral anticoagulation, limiting inference for catheter-based LAAO.
appraisal.one_line: LAAOS III: surgical left atrial appendage occlusion during cardiac surgery lowered stroke or systemic embolism in patients with atrial fibrillation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Stroke or systemic embolism occurred in 114 participants (4.8%) in the occlusion group and 168 (7.0%) in the no-occlusion group (hazard ratio, 0.67; 95% confidence interval, 0.53 to 0.85; P = 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adequately powered randomised evidence for appendage occlusion on top of anticoagulation, relevant to LAAO policy.

title: Ultrasound renal denervation for hypertension resistant to a triple medication pill (RADIANCE-HTN TRIO): a randomised, multicentre, single-blind, sham-controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, single-blind, sham-controlled trial; 989 enrolled, 136 randomised (renal denervation 69, sham 67).
appraisal.main_limitation: Blood pressure surrogate at 2 months in a small randomised sample; industry funded.
appraisal.one_line: RADIANCE-HTN TRIO: ultrasound renal denervation lowered daytime ambulatory systolic pressure more than sham in resistant hypertension at 2 months.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Daytime ambulatory systolic blood pressure fell -8.0 mm Hg [IQR -16.4 to 0.0] vs -3.0 mm Hg [-10.3 to 1.8]; median between-group difference -4.5 mm Hg [95% CI -8.5 to -0.3]; adjusted p=0.022.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adjacent device indication in resistant hypertension with sham control.

title: Amplatzer Amulet Left Atrial Appendage Occluder Versus Watchman Device for Stroke Prophylaxis (Amulet IDE): A Randomized, Controlled Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 1878 patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation.
appraisal.main_limitation: Device-versus-device comparison without an anticoagulation or no-closure arm.
appraisal.one_line: Amulet IDE found the Amulet left atrial appendage occluder noninferior to Watchman for safety and stroke prevention, with more procedural complications.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary safety end point was 14.5% vs. 14.7% (difference=-0.14 [95% CI, -3.42 to 3.13]; P<0.001 for noninferiority); the primary effectiveness end point was 2.8% vs. 2.8% (difference=0.00 [95% CI, -1.55 to 1.55]). Procedure-related complications were 4.5% vs. 2.5%.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides head-to-head evidence between the two main appendage occluders in an adjacent intervention.

title: Amulet or Watchman Device for Percutaneous Left Atrial Appendage Closure: Primary Results of the SWISS-APERO Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised open-label trial, 221 patients at 8 European centres.
appraisal.main_limitation: Imaging surrogate primary endpoint and short follow-up of 45 days.
appraisal.one_line: SWISS-APERO found no difference in a composite of crossover or residual appendage patency between Amulet and Watchman at 45 days, with more procedural complications with Amulet.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 71 (67.6%) patients receiving Amulet and 70 (70.0%) receiving Watchman (risk ratio, 0.97 [95% CI, 0.80-1.16]; P=0.713). Major procedure-related complications were 9.0% vs. 2.7% (P=0.047).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Head-to-head device data in an adjacent intervention, with a safety signal for Amulet.

title: Heterogeneity of Treatment Effects in an Analysis of Pooled Individual Patient Data From Randomized Trials of Device Closure of Patent Foramen Ovale After Stroke.

appraisal.design_and_n: IPD pooled analysis of 6 randomised trials, 3740 participants; median follow-up 57 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis of pooled trials with few events (121).
appraisal.one_line: Pooled individual patient data from six PFO closure trials found that benefit on recurrent stroke varied by RoPE score and PASCAL category.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Annualised stroke incidence was 1.09% (95% CI, 0.88%-1.36%) with medical therapy and 0.47% (95% CI, 0.35%-0.65%) with closure (adjusted HR, 0.41 [95% CI, 0.28-0.60]). PASCAL unlikely, possible and probable categories had HRs of 1.14 (95% CI, 0.53-2.46), 0.38 (95% CI, 0.22-0.65) and 0.10 (95% CI, 0.03-0.35) (P for interaction = .003).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Individualises selection for PFO closure and is an example of IPD analysis of treatment-effect heterogeneity.

title: Atrial shunt device for heart failure with preserved and mildly reduced ejection fraction (REDUCE LAP-HF II): a randomised, multicentre, blinded, sham-controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised sham-controlled trial, 626 participants (314 device, 312 sham) at 89 centres.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup signals of harm (higher pulmonary artery pressure, men) are exploratory.
appraisal.one_line: REDUCE LAP-HF II found no benefit of an atrial shunt device in heart failure with ejection fraction of at least 40%.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: There were no differences between groups in the primary composite endpoint (win ratio 1·0 [95% CI 0·8-1·2]; p=0·85).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Neutral result for a prominent interventional heart failure device.

title: Long-term outcomes after catheter-based renal artery denervation for resistant hypertension: final follow-up of the randomised SYMPLICITY HTN-3 Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Single-blind, multicentre, sham-controlled randomised trial in 88 US centres; 535 patients randomly assigned (364 denervation, 171 sham).
appraisal.main_limitation: Sham patients could cross over after 6 months and their values were imputed, with substantial attrition in 36-month follow-up data.
appraisal.one_line: Final 36-month follow-up of the sham-controlled SYMPLICITY HTN-3 trial reported larger blood pressure reductions with renal denervation than sham, with similar adverse event rates.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 36 months, the change in office systolic blood pressure was -26·4 mm Hg (SD 25·9) in the renal artery denervation group and -5·7 mm Hg (24·4) in the sham control group (adjusted treatment difference -22·1 mm Hg [95% CI -27·2 to -17·0]; p≤0·0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Long-term durability data for renal denervation in resistant hypertension (D9), a population where the original primary endpoint was neutral.

title: Renal denervation in the management of hypertension in adults. A clinical consensus statement of the ESC Council on Hypertension and the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI).

appraisal.design_and_n: Clinical consensus statement by an expert group of the ESC Council on Hypertension and EAPCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus recommendations rest on trials with blood pressure rather than clinical outcome endpoints.
appraisal.one_line: ESC and EAPCI clinical consensus statement positioning renal denervation as an adjunct option in uncontrolled resistant hypertension.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: New society guidance on a device therapy with major implications for interventional practice and patient selection.

title: Endovascular Ultrasound Renal Denervation to Treat Hypertension: The RADIANCE II Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Sham-controlled randomised trial at 37 US and 24 European centres; 150 patients randomised to ultrasound renal denervation and 74 to a sham procedure.
appraisal.main_limitation: Blood pressure surrogate endpoint at 2 months with no clinical outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: Sham-controlled trial of ultrasound renal denervation off medication in hypertension.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Baseline-adjusted between-group difference in daytime ambulatory SBP was -6.3 mm Hg [95% CI, -9.3 to -3.2 mm Hg], P < .001; no major adverse events were reported in either group.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds sham-controlled efficacy data for a device therapy at the periphery of interventional practice.

title: Network Meta-Analysis of Initial Antithrombotic Regimens After Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Network meta-analysis of 41 studies comprising 12,451 patients with nonvalvular AF.
appraisal.main_limitation: Included studies are largely observational with indirect comparisons, so confounding and heterogeneity are likely.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis of initial antithrombotic regimens after left atrial appendage occlusion.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: DOAC was associated with lower all-cause mortality than VKA (OR: 0.39; 95% CI: 0.17-0.89; P = 0.03), and DAPT was associated with fewer thromboembolic events than SAPT (OR: 0.50; 95% CI: 0.29-0.88; P = 0.02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses an area with little randomised evidence for post-LAAO antithrombotic therapy.

title: Oral Anticoagulation Use and Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion in LAAOS III.

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of a randomised trial, including 3027 patients on a vitamin K antagonist and 879 on a direct oral anticoagulant at discharge.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc subgroups by post-randomisation OAC use are not randomised.
appraisal.one_line: Analysis of oral anticoagulant use and the effect of left atrial appendage occlusion in LAAOS III.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The effect of LAA occlusion on ischemic stroke or systemic embolism was consistent after discharge across the 3 OAC groups: hazard ratios of 0.70 (95% CI, 0.51-0.96), 0.63 (95% CI, 0.43-0.94), and 0.76 (95% CI, 0.32-1.79).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports surgical LAA occlusion on top of anticoagulation and informs the interventional LAAO debate.

title: Concomitant Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion and Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement Among Patients With Atrial Fibrillation.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 349 patients enrolled (177 TAVR + LAAO and 172 TAVR + medical therapy) at 34 US centers.
appraisal.main_limitation: Noninferiority design with limited sample size and added procedural complexity.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of concomitant LAAO with TAVR versus TAVR with medical therapy in patients with atrial fibrillation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: For the composite primary end point, TAVR + LAAO was noninferior to TAVR + medical therapy (22.7 versus 27.3 events per 100 patient-years; hazard ratio, 0.86 [95% CI, 0.60-1.22]; Pnoninferiority<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs antithrombotic strategy and device combination in TAVR patients with AF.

title: Residual leaks following percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion and outcomes: a meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: 48 eligible studies (44 non-randomized/observational and 4 randomized studies) including 61 666 patients with atrial fibrillation who underwent left atrial appendage occlusion
appraisal.main_limitation: Pooled data are almost entirely from non-randomised studies, so the associations are open to confounding and heterogeneity in leak definitions.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of 48 studies finds that transoesophageal peri-device leak after LAAO is associated with thromboembolism, whereas CT-detected leaks are not.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: TEE-based PDL was associated with thromboembolism (pooled odds ratio (pOR) 2.04, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.52-2.74), all-cause mortality (pOR 1.16, 95% CI: 1.08-1.24), and major bleeding (pOR 1.12, 95% CI: 1.03-1.22), compared with no reported PDL.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Gives graded prognostic data on leak size that bear on imaging follow-up and antithrombotic decisions after LAAO.

title: Coronary sinus reducer for the treatment of refractory angina (ORBITA-COSMIC): a randomised, placebo-controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: 51 patients randomly assigned (CSR n=25, placebo n=26) in a blinded Bayesian trial at six UK hospitals.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small sample, six-month follow-up and symptom endpoints with two embolisation events in the device group.
appraisal.one_line: ORBITA-COSMIC found the coronary sinus reducer improved angina episodes but not myocardial blood flow compared with placebo.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Myocardial blood flow in ischaemic segments did not improve with CSR compared with placebo (difference 0·06 mL/min per g [95% CrI -0·09 to 0·20]; Pr(Benefit)=78·8%). The number of daily angina episodes was reduced with CSR compared with placebo (OR 1·40 [95% CrI 1·08 to 1·83]; Pr(Benefit)=99·4%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: First blinded sham-controlled evidence for the coronary sinus reducer, relevant to refractory angina options.

title: Interatrial Shunt Treatment for Heart Failure: The Randomized RELIEVE-HF Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: 508 patients randomised at 94 sites in 11 countries to interatrial shunt treatment (n=250) or a placebo procedure (n=258).
appraisal.main_limitation: The ejection fraction subgroup findings were prespecified as hypothesis-generating, and the primary outcome was neutral.
appraisal.one_line: RELIEVE-HF found interatrial shunt implantation did not improve the hierarchical outcome in heart failure, with opposite signals by ejection fraction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: There was no difference in the 2-year primary effectiveness outcome between the shunt and placebo procedure groups (win ratio, 0.86 [95% CI, 0.61-1.22]; P=0.20). Patients with reduced LVEF had fewer adverse cardiovascular events with shunt treatment versus placebo (annualized rate 49.0% versus 88.6%; relative risk, 0.55 [95% CI, 0.42-0.73]; P<0.0001), whereas patients with preserved LVEF had more cardiovascular events with shunt treatment (annualized rate 60.2% versus 35.9%; relative risk, 1.68 [95% CI, 1.29-2.19]; P=0.0001; Pinteraction<0.0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses an adjacent interventional heart failure device and identifies a possible harm in preserved ejection fraction.

title: Effects of Catheter-Based Renal Denervation in Hypertension: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis; Ten trials comprising 2478 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Study-level data with significant heterogeneity between trials and few safety events, so safety estimates are imprecise.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of sham-controlled renal denervation trials reporting blood pressure reduction without excess safety events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: RDN reduced 24-hour and office systolic blood pressure by 4.4 mm Hg (95% CI, 2.7 to 6.1; P<0.00001) and 6.6 mm Hg (95% CI, 3.6 to 9.7; P<0.0001), respectively. All-cause death odds ratio, 1.76 [95% CI, 0.34 to 9.20].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Pools the sham-controlled evidence on renal denervation, a lower-weight adjacent domain, with surrogate blood pressure endpoints.

title: Large-Bore Mechanical Thrombectomy Versus Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis in the Management of Intermediate-Risk Pulmonary Embolism: Primary Results of the PEERLESS Randomized Controlled Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized controlled trial; 550 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: The win ratio is driven largely by clinical deterioration and ICU use, which are open to bias in an unblinded comparison, and there was no difference in hard outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: PEERLESS found large-bore mechanical thrombectomy superior to catheter-directed thrombolysis on a hierarchical win-ratio composite in intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism, with no difference in mortality or bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred significantly less frequently with LBMT compared with CDT (win ratio, 5.01 [95% CI, 3.68-6.97]; P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: First randomized comparison of two catheter-based pulmonary embolism strategies, relevant to a lower-weight adjacent domain.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure after Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: International randomized trial; 1600 patients (803 closure, 797 anticoagulation).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design in post-ablation patients only, with industry funding.
appraisal.one_line: OPTION found left atrial appendage closure after AF ablation reduced bleeding versus anticoagulation and was non-inferior for death, stroke or systemic embolism.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 36 months, a primary safety end-point event had occurred in 65 patients (8.5%) in the left atrial appendage closure group (device group) and in 137 patients (18.1%) in the anticoagulation group (P<0.001 for superiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports an alternative to long-term anticoagulation after AF ablation, an adjacent domain.

title: 5-Year Results From the AMPLATZER Amulet Left Atrial Appendage Occluder Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized trial extended follow-up; 1,878 patients randomized.
appraisal.main_limitation: Secondary long-term report with open-label elements.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year Amulet IDE results show similar clinical outcomes to Watchman, with more patients free of oral anticoagulation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The composite of ischemic stroke or systemic embolism (7.4% vs 7.1%; P = 0.851); major bleeding (20.1% vs 20.0%; P = 0.882); all-cause death (28.7% vs 31.1%; P = 0.217).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs choice between two left atrial appendage occluders.

title: Outcomes of Percutaneous Mechanical Aspiration in Right-Sided Infective Endocarditis: A Multicenter Registry.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective multicentre registry, 256 patients from 19 institutions.
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective, uncontrolled and based on site-reported vegetation size, so comparison with medical or surgical management is not possible.
appraisal.one_line: Multicentre registry of percutaneous mechanical aspiration for right-sided infective endocarditis reports high procedural success with substantial in-hospital events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Procedural success was achieved in 89.4%; the primary endpoint occurred in 18% (mortality: 9.8%; new PE: 8.3%; emergency surgery: 3.1%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Largest series of this emerging catheter-based debulking approach, informing safety expectations before any randomised comparison.

title: Surgical left atrial appendage occlusion in valvular heart disease without atrial fibrillation: the OPINION trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre open-label randomised superiority trial, 2118 participants in the intention-to-treat population (1062 SLAAO, 1056 control).
appraisal.main_limitation: One-year follow-up in an open-label trial of three Chinese centres, with fewer events than expected.
appraisal.one_line: OPINION found prophylactic surgical left atrial appendage occlusion did not significantly reduce stroke, TIA or cardiovascular death in valve surgery patients without AF.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 1-year primary endpoint occurred in 73 (6.9%) patients in the SLAAO group and in 87 (8.2%) patients in the control group (hazard ratio 0.83; 95% confidence interval 0.61-1.14; P = .25).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs appendage occlusion in patients without AF, a population not covered by earlier trials.

title: Short-Term Anticoagulation Versus Dual Antiplatelet Therapy for Preventing Device Thrombosis Following Left Atrial Appendage Closure: The ANDES Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective multicentre randomised trial, 510 patients (253 DOAC, 257 DAPT); 399 had TEE at 60 days on allocated treatment.
appraisal.main_limitation: Primary analysis was per-protocol on patients with TEE, and the trial was not powered for clinical events.
appraisal.one_line: ANDES found short-term DOAC did not significantly reduce device thrombosis after LAAC versus DAPT but lowered a composite safety outcome, driven by bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome occurred in 3 patients (1.5%) in the DOAC group compared with 8 patients (4.1%) in the DAPT group (difference, -2.7% [95% CI, -6.0% to 0.6%]; P=0.110).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides randomised data on post-LAAC antithrombotic therapy, an area with limited evidence.

title: Randomized Controlled Trial of Mechanical Thrombectomy With Anticoagulation Versus Anticoagulation Alone for Acute Intermediate-High Risk Pulmonary Embolism: Primary Outcomes From the STORM-PE Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: International randomised controlled trial, 100 patients at 22 sites (CAVT n=47; anticoagulation alone n=53).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small trial with an imaging surrogate as primary endpoint rather than clinical outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: STORM-PE, the first randomised trial of mechanical thrombectomy plus anticoagulation in intermediate-high risk pulmonary embolism, reported greater early RV/LV ratio reduction with thrombectomy.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 48 hours, mean reduction in RV/LV ratio was greater for CAVT (0.52±0.37) than anticoagulation (0.24±0.40).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Randomised evidence on catheter-directed therapy for pulmonary embolism, an adjacent intervention with little trial data.

title: 2026 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ACEP/CHEST/SCAI/SHM/SIR/SVM/SVN Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Acute Pulmonary Embolism in Adults: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines.

appraisal.design_and_n: Clinical practice guideline; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Abstract does not state individual recommendation classes or levels, which must be taken from the full text.
appraisal.one_line: New de novo 2026 AHA/ACC multisociety guideline for acute pulmonary embolism introducing clinical categories and covering advanced interventional therapies.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets US guidance on catheter-directed therapy and risk categorisation in pulmonary embolism, an adjacent intervention area.

title: 2026 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ACEP/CHEST/SCAI/SHM/SIR/SVM/SVN Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Acute Pulmonary Embolism in Adults: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Clinical practice guideline; literature search from February 2024 to October 2024, with select key studies up to April 2025.
appraisal.main_limitation: Abstract describes scope and structure only; individual recommendation classes are not given.
appraisal.one_line: New de novo joint AHA/ACC guideline for acute pulmonary embolism in adults, introducing clinical categories for severity and management.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets the US position on risk categorisation and advanced therapy for acute PE, relevant to catheter-directed treatment decisions.

title: Mechanical Thrombectomy and Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis in Acute Pulmonary Embolism: Trends and Practice Patterns in the PERT Consortium Registry (2016-2024).
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective registry of 2,958 patients with intermediate- or high-risk PE treated with advanced therapies at 48 US institutions, 2016 to 2024.
appraisal.main_limitation: Descriptive registry of practice patterns with no outcome comparison between devices.
appraisal.one_line: PERT Consortium registry traces the shift from catheter-directed thrombolysis to mechanical thrombectomy for acute PE.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The use of MT increased by 18% per year (incident rate ratio [IRR]: 1.18; 95% CI: 1.14-1.23), surpassing CDT use by 2021, whereas the use of CDT and systemic thrombolysis declined by 13% and 12% per year, respectively.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Documents rapid adoption of catheter therapy for PE in the absence of randomised outcome evidence.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure or Medical Therapy in Atrial Fibrillation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised noninferiority trial in Germany; 912 patients randomised, 446 device and 442 medical therapy analysed.
appraisal.main_limitation: Broad composite primary endpoint and open-label comparison with heterogeneous medical care.
appraisal.one_line: Left atrial appendage closure was not shown to be noninferior to physician-directed best medical care in AF patients at high stroke and bleeding risk.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: First primary end-point event in 155 patients (incidence per 100 patient-years, 16.8) in the device group and 127 patients (incidence per 100 patient-years, 13.3) in the medical-therapy group (difference in restricted mean survival time, -0.36 years; 95% confidence interval, -0.70 to -0.01; P = 0.44 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tempers enthusiasm for LAAO as a substitute for medical therapy in high-risk patients.

title: Ultrasound-Facilitated, Catheter-Directed Fibrinolysis for Acute Pulmonary Embolism.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multinational adaptive-design randomised trial with blinded adjudication; 544 patients (273 intervention, 271 control).
appraisal.main_limitation: Effect driven mainly by cardiorespiratory decompensation or collapse, with a 7-day horizon and numerically more major bleeding.
appraisal.one_line: Ultrasound-facilitated catheter-directed fibrinolysis plus anticoagulation reduced early clinical deterioration in intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary-outcome event in 11 patients (4.0%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.3 to 7.1) vs 28 (10.3%; 95% CI, 7.2 to 14.5) (relative risk, 0.39; 95% CI, 0.20 to 0.77; P = 0.005).
appraisal.why_it_matters: First randomised evidence of clinical benefit for catheter-directed therapy in intermediate-risk PE.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure or Anticoagulation for Atrial Fibrillation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: International randomised noninferiority trial; 3000 patients (1499 device, 1501 anticoagulation).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label device versus drug comparison with an industry sponsor and a wide noninferiority margin.
appraisal.one_line: In anticoagulation-eligible AF patients, left atrial appendage closure was noninferior to NOAC therapy for the efficacy composite and reduced non-procedure-related bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary efficacy event in 81 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 5.7%) vs 65 patients (4.8%) (difference, 0.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.8 to 2.6; P<0.001 for noninferiority); non-procedure-related bleeding hazard ratio, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.45 to 0.67.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Extends LAAO evidence to patients suitable for anticoagulation and may shift guideline positions.

title: Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis in Intermediate-High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 558 patients (280 thrombolysis, 278 standard care).
appraisal.main_limitation: Seven-day primary outcome driven by cardiorespiratory decompensation.
appraisal.one_line: Catheter-directed thrombolysis plus anticoagulation reduced early death, recurrence or decompensation in intermediate-high-risk PE.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary-outcome event in 2 patients (0.7%) vs 19 (6.8%) (relative risk, 0.10; 95% confidence interval, 0.02 to 0.44; P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Second large trial supporting catheter-directed therapy in intermediate-high-risk PE.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure Versus Oral Anticoagulation for Prevention of Stroke or Systemic Embolism in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation: An Updated Meta-Analysis of 7004 Patients Across Six Randomized Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of RCTs; 6 RCTs (n = 7004 patients).
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract does not describe trial heterogeneity or certainty of evidence.
appraisal.one_line: A meta-analysis of six randomised trials comparing left atrial appendage closure with oral anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The risk of stroke or systemic embolism (SSE) did not differ significantly between the LAAC and OAC groups (RR: 1.10 [0.87-1.39]; p = 0.42). The risk of ischemic SSE was significantly increased with LAAC (RR: 1.41 [1.07-1.85]; p = 0.02) compared with OAC.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It bears on the use of LAAC as an alternative to anticoagulation and shows a possible excess of ischaemic events.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure or Medical Therapy in Atrial Fibrillation: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of RCTs; five randomized controlled trials, 5,404 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Noninferiority was not met for several efficacy outcomes, with wide intervals.
appraisal.one_line: A meta-analysis of five randomised trials testing noninferiority of left atrial appendage closure against medical therapy in atrial fibrillation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: LAAC met noninferiority compared with medical therapy in atrial fibrillation for major bleeding (RR 0.86; 95% CI 0.59-1.26) and all-cause mortality (RR 0.93; 95% CI 0.71-1.22).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It overlaps with other recent LAAC pooled analyses and informs the choice between closure and anticoagulation.

title: Long-Term Safety and Procedural Performance of an Interatrial Shunt for Heart Failure According to Ejection Fraction.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised sham-controlled trial, prespecified LVEF-stratified safety analysis; 605 enrolled patients (508 randomised; 97 roll-in), shunt attempted in 370.
appraisal.main_limitation: Safety subanalysis of a trial; the abstract gives no effect estimates for the phenotype-specific comparisons.
appraisal.one_line: Two-year safety and durability of an interatrial shunt in RELIEVE-HF, stratified by ejection fraction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: No device- or procedure-related MACNE occurred through 2 years (0%; 95% CI: 0%-0.9%), and shunt patency was 99.4% (95% CI: 97.9%-99.9%). In HFpEF, shunt therapy was associated with higher all-cause MACNE, greater SAE burden, increased major bleeding, and greater renal decline.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Indicates harm signals with shunting in HFpEF and supports phenotype-specific use of interatrial shunts.

title: Percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion versus oral anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation: A pragmatic meta-analysis of randomized trials within the DOAC era.
journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of randomised trials; four trials comprising 5890 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Few trials with wide confidence intervals; Mantel-Haenszel pooling with a 'pragmatic' framework and some outcomes drawn from protocol-defined datasets.
appraisal.one_line: Pragmatic meta-analysis of randomised trials comparing LAAO with oral anticoagulation in a DOAC-predominant setting found no significant difference in hard endpoints.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Overall stroke (RR 1.18, 95% CI 0.87-1.60; p = 0.28), major bleeding (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.81-1.19; p = 0.85) and all-cause mortality (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.85-1.17; p = 0.99) did not differ significantly; ischemic stroke was RR 1.36, 95% CI 0.99-1.89; p = 0.06.
appraisal.why_it_matters: LAAO versus DOAC remains contested, and the ischaemic stroke signal bears on D9 practice and on the case for further trials.

title: Safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System in acute intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism: the SPIRARE II pivotal trial.
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective single-arm multicentre pivotal investigation (NCT06576427) at 19 sites; 123 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: No control group and a surrogate imaging co-primary endpoint.
appraisal.one_line: Single-arm pivotal study of a mechanical aspiration thrombectomy system in intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism (adjacent domain).
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In 123 patients, the 48-hour composite MAE rate was 2.4% (3/123), meeting the prespecified performance goal (one-sided p<0.0001). The mean RV/LV diameter ratio decreased from 1.44±0.33 at baseline to 1.05±0.21 at 48 hours.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Device evidence for catheter-directed PE therapy, where randomised outcome data remain awaited.
